displayPattern: 7-segment display on a Trane S9V2 two-stage variable-speed furnace (Service Facts S9V2-SF-2A-EN): E2.3
meaning: 1st stage gas valve not energized: it failed 10 times in the same call for heat. The service facts say 24 VAC was not sensed on MVL those 10 times.
causes: 24 VAC not sensed on the 1st stage gas valve (MVL) ten times in one heat call
diySteps: Do not jumper the gas valve to force heat
Technician: the Service Facts step for fault 2.3 is to replace the integrated furnace control (IFC)
proAdvice: Call a licensed HVAC technician. The Service Facts flowchart for fault 2.3 says 24 VAC was not sensed on MVL ten times in the same call for heat, and the step is to replace the integrated furnace control. It does not say to replace the gas valve. The American Standard installer's guide states the same alarm and does not name that part. E2.3 is not retry lockout E2.1.
safetyNote: If you smell gas, do not touch any electrical switch or use a phone in the building; leave immediately and call your gas supplier from outside. Turn off electrical power at the furnace switch or breaker before opening any panel, and never bypass or jumper a limit, rollout or pressure switch. Gas valve, burner, venting, wiring and control-board work should be done by a licensed HVAC technician.
sourceTitle: Trane S9V2 Service Facts S9V2-SF-2A-EN (04 Mar 2021), troubleshooting section. Read 2026-11-07
